specification: Implement a role-based permission checker as the package rbac, consisting of three editable modules (rbac/patterns.py, rbac/roles.py, rbac/policy.py) plus an empty rbac/__init__.py that must not be edited. rbac/patterns.py defines validate_pattern(pattern), validate_permission(permission) and matches(pattern, permission). A permission is a str of one or more segments joined by ':' (for example 'doc:read'); every segment is one or more characters from lowercase a-z, digits 0-9, '_' and '-'. validate_permission raises TypeError if its argument is not a str and ValueError if it is empty or has any segment that is empty or contains other characters (so a wildcard is not a valid permission). A pattern is also a ':'-joined str whose segments are either valid permission segments, or the segment '*', or the segment '**' which is allowed only as the last segment. validate_pattern raises TypeError for a non-str and ValueError for an empty str or any invalid segment. matches(pattern, permission) validates the pattern first and the permission second (raising as described) and returns a bool: a '*' segment matches exactly one segment of any content, a literal segment matches only an equal segment (case-sensitive), and a final '**' segment matches one or more remaining segments, at least one. Without a final '**' the pattern and the permission must have the same number of segments. For example 'doc:*' matches 'doc:read' but neither 'doc' nor 'doc:read:all', 'doc:**' matches 'doc:read' and 'doc:read:all' but not 'doc', and '**' matches every valid permission. rbac/roles.py defines class RoleSet, which starts empty. add_role(name, allow=(), deny=(), revoke=(), inherits=()) defines a role. Checks run in this order: name must be a nonempty str (TypeError, ValueError); a name that is already defined raises ValueError; then allow, deny and revoke in that order, each of which must be a list or tuple (TypeError) of valid patterns (ValueError for an invalid pattern, TypeError for a non-str item, as validate_pattern does); then inherits must be a list or tuple (TypeError) whose items are the names of already defined roles (TypeError for a non-str item, ValueError for an empty or undefined name). A call that raises changes nothing. add_inheritance(child, parent) makes the existing role child also inherit from the existing role parent: both names are checked in that order (TypeError for a non-str, ValueError for an empty or undefined name); if child equals parent, or parent already inherits from child directly or through other roles, it raises ValueError and changes nothing; adding an edge that already exists is allowed and changes nothing. effective(name) returns a tuple (allow, deny) of two frozensets of pattern strings, always reflecting the current definitions and edges, with the same name checks as above. For a role, first take the union of the allow sets and, separately, the union of the deny sets of all roles it inherits from (each computed by the same rules, recursively); then remove from that inherited allow union every pattern string that is equal to one of the role's own revoke patterns (a revoke removes only identical pattern strings, so revoking 'doc:read' does not remove 'doc:*', and it never affects deny sets); then add the role's own allow patterns to the allow set and its own deny patterns to the deny set. A pattern that a role revokes and also lists in its own allow stays allowed. An inherited pattern that is revoked in one inheritance branch but still reaches the role through another branch stays allowed. rbac/policy.py defines class Policy(roles), which wraps a RoleSet and starts with no assignments. assign(user, role) gives the user the role: user must be a nonempty str (TypeError, ValueError), then role is checked like a role name in RoleSet (TypeError for a non-str, ValueError for an empty or undefined name); assigning the same role twice has no further effect. unassign(user, role) removes an assignment: user is checked as above, a non-str role raises TypeError, and a role that is not currently assigned to the user raises ValueError. user_roles(user) returns the user's assigned role names as a new list sorted in ascending order (empty for a user without roles). explain(user, permission) checks user as above, then permission with validate_permission, and takes the union of the effective allow sets and the union of the effective deny sets of all the user's assigned roles, looked up at call time. Deny overrides allow across all of the user's roles regardless of their order: if any deny pattern in the union matches the permission, the result is {'allowed': False, 'decision': 'deny', 'by': deny_patterns}, where deny_patterns is the sorted list of the matching deny patterns; otherwise if any allow pattern matches it is {'allowed': True, 'decision': 'allow', 'by': allow_patterns} with the sorted list of the matching allow patterns; otherwise it is {'allowed': False, 'decision': 'default', 'by': []}. Sorting is plain ascending str order. A user who has never been assigned a role gets the default result. is_allowed(user, permission) returns the 'allowed' value of explain. Exception messages are not specified.
